main_text: Home . Projects . GÉANT EOSC Node GÉANT EOSC Node The GÉANT EOSC Node is GÉANT's contribution to the EOSC Federation, providing trusted digital infrastructure that enables researchers across Europe to discover, access and use research resources seamlessly. GÉANT Service Catalogue The catalogue provides an overview of the GÉANT services onboarded into the EOSC Federation. EOSC Federation An evolving European federation enabling researchers to discover, access, share and reuse data and resources. EOSC Nodes A ‘system of systems’ to find and access data and services for research and innovation in Europe. GÉANT Compendium Explore GÉANT Compendium data and reports. GÉANT eAcademy An online learning space for the research and education community. GÉANT and the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) A federated European Open Science Cloud can only thrive if researchers can connect, collaborate and access resources seamlessly. GÉANT provides the trusted digital foundations that help make this possible. EOSC is an evolving federation of digital infrastructures and services that enables researchers across Europe to discover, access, share and reuse research data and resources across disciplines and borders. As the pan-European network for research and education, GÉANT plays a key role in supporting this vision. Together with National Research and Education Networks (NRENs) and partners across Europe, GÉANT contributes trusted connectivity, identity and access management, cybersecurity, cloud integration and other core services that underpin a secure and interoperable EOSC Federation. Our involvement extends across a range of European projects that help shape, build and operate EOSC. Through these initiatives, GÉANT contributes technical expertise, community engagement and long-term sustainability, ensuring that researchers benefit from seamless access to the services, data and collaboration opportunities they need to advance science. A pan-European e-infrastructure Node The EOSC Federation is built on trusted Nodes. The GÉANT EOSC Node contributes the connectivity, trust services and expertise that help make federation work. Building on GÉANT’s long-standing expertise in networking, identity and trust services, the Node delivers core capabilities that support interoperability across the EOSC Federation, including authentication and authorisation, secure access, federation services and high-performance connectivity. GÉANT works alongside NRENs and European partners to connect national and thematic EOSC Nodes into a secure, scalable and interoperable ecosystem. For NRENs, the GÉANT EOSC Node also provides a gateway to the EOSC Federation. Organisations that are not yet participating through a national Node can onboard their services via the GÉANT Node as resource providers or use it to connect users with services and resources on demand. The GÉANT EOSC Node builds on a series of major milestones, including the launch of the EOSC EU Node in 2024, the EOSC Federation in 2025 and the EuroHPC Federation Platform in 2026, all contributing to a unified, secure and user-friendly environment for accessing Europe’s research and computing resources. What the GÉANT Node enables The GÉANT Node acts as a gateway between the EOSC Federation and the services, resources and expertise of Europe’s research and education networking community. Here are four examples of how it can make federated access and collaboration a reality. Federated access to EOSC The GÉANT Node will provide the technical solution for the Trust & Identity layer of the EOSC Federation through MyAccessID. It will connect national and institutional identities, enabling secure authentication and Single Sign-On across EOSC Nodes and services. Value to users: Researchers and service providers can use their trusted identities to access EOSC services and resources seamlessly, securely and interoperably. Access to European cloud resources The GÉANT Node will make cloud resources from the OCRE Framework available through the EOSC Federation, connecting researchers and research infrastructures with European cloud providers. Value to users: Easier access to European cloud resources, lowering barriers to cloud adoption while supporting European digital sovereignty. NREN resources through the GÉANT Node The GÉANT Node will act as a gateway for NRENs that are not themselves EOSC Nodes, enabling them to make selected services and resources available through the EOSC Federation. Value to users: A wider range of services and resources becomes accessible through EOSC, while making it easier for NRENs to contribute their capabilities to the Federation. Connecting EOSC and EuroHPC The GÉANT Node will demonstrate how EOSC and EuroHPC can work together through federated identity and Single Sign-On. The use case will connect research data, EOSC services, cloud resources and EuroHPC computing in a seamless research workflow. Value to users: Researchers can move securely between EOSC and EuroHPC resources, enabling data to be processed on European supercomputing infrastructure and the results stored and analysed through EOSC services. GÉANT Service Catalogue In short The GÉANT Node offers network, security, and Identity and Access Management services to the European research community. It enables organisations to establish compliant EOSC Nodes and provides access to services and resources from GÉANT members, including cloud resources, NREN services, AAI federation and links between EOSC and EuroHPC. Related pages EuroHPC HyperConnectivity GÉANT has been awarded a contract by the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking (JU). Membership The GÉANT Association includes 37 NRENs, NORDUnet, and associates including five Nordic NRENs, KREN, CERN, and ESA. Contact To find out more about the GÉANT EOSC Node get in touch via the contact form.

What is GÉANT and what does it do? The GÉANT Association is a membership of 37 European National Research and Education Networks (NRENs) and one Nordic representative member. For decades, we have been building physical and human networks across Europe and around the world. Our unique collaboration model delivers an unmatched multiplier effect and creates the digital foundation for research and education in Europe. Together, and as a trusted partner of the European Commission, we power the knowledge sharing and innovation essential for strengthening Europe’s competitiveness, security, and prosperity. Find out more about GÉANT. 02. I have a question about GÉANT, but I don’t know who to contact. Fill in the form on this page selecting the option “General enquiries”. We will put you in contact with the relevant team at GÉANT! 03. What services does GÉANT provide? GÉANT delivers the pan-European GÉANT network for scientific excellence, research, education and innovation, as well as an integrated catalogue of connectivity, Identity and Access Management (IAM), cloud, and security services. 04. Does GÉANT work with organisations outside Europe? Yes, through extensive global partnerships, and thanks to funding from the European Commission, GÉANT interconnects over 110 countries worldwide. 05. Where can I find the new GÉANT logo, as well as GÉANT materials and resources? Visit the GÉANT Resources website, bringing together a growing range of documents and materials to support our members and partners. resources.geant.org

children.title: Vision, mission, strategy - GÉANT
children.main_text: Home . About GÉANT . Vision, mission, strategy Vision, mission, strategy The GÉANT Association provides and advances the digital infrastructure and services required to accelerate research, education, and innovation for a secure and competitive Europe. Membership The GÉANT Association includes 37 NRENs, NORDUnet, and associates including five Nordic NRENs, KREN, CERN, and ESA. Governance The General Assembly is the GÉANT Association’s highest governing body, consisting of representatives from each member. Projects GÉANT projects drive innovation across networking, Identity and Access Management (IAM), global collaboration and more. Vision and mission The GÉANT Association consists of 43 European National Research and Education Networks (NRENs). For decades, we have been building physical and human networks across Europe and around the world. Our unique collaboration model delivers an unmatched multiplier effect and creates the digital foundation for research and education (R&E) in Europe. Together, and as a trusted partner of the European Commission, we power the knowledge sharing and innovation essential for strengthening Europe’s competitiveness, security, and prosperity. Our vision Powering Knowledge for Europe. Our mission The GÉANT Association provides and advances the digital infrastructure and services required to accelerate research, education, and innovation for a secure and competitive Europe. GÉANT Association Strategy 2026-2030 Strategic goals Collaborate to strengthen physical and human networks across Europe and beyond We will further strengthen collaboration between our unique and diverse human network – the most effective way to achieve not just the highest quality and geographic reach of the physical network, but the advancement of the entire digital foundation for research and education. Create scalable, innovative services prioritised by the community We will identify, co-create, and deliver digital services that integrate emerging technology to comprehensively address community priorities, while linking seamlessly to the digital infrastructure we provide. Build a sustainable financial model We will build a sustainable financial model that allows the GÉANT Association to continue its core operations, expand to new markets and end users, realise healthy service and product life cycles, and thrive in a rapidly advancing and commercially competitive technology landscape. Challenges The challenges we face as the GÉANT Association are not static. These are the current primary uncertainties, challenges or risks, and they will be monitored and updated annually: Geopolitical uncertainty with the risk of fragmentation. A diverse association with a spectrum of needs. A highly uncertain funding landscape. A changing EU regulatory environment​. Evolving technology and user expectations. Transformations To both achieve our strategic goals and mitigate challenges, we strive to reach the following transformations by 2030: Realise platforms for NREN collaboration that facilitate both unity and NREN to NREN mutual benefit.​ Ensure organisational and association resilience through a sustainable business and governance model. ​ Establish and execute a common vision on services and innovation with equal access across Europe and globally.​ Leverage our unique position in Europe to increase visibility and influence policy. ​ Mainstream a proactive mindset and approach to anticipate and mitigate future uncertainties. GÉANT Association Strategy Framework 2026-2030 The GÉANT Association Strategy 2026-2030 is underpinned by this Strategy Framework that further elaborates on the strategy and provides the framework for joint execution by the association . It also supports the creation of roadmaps and annual plans which inform the Annual Operating Plan and Budget. Guiding principles The GÉANT Association’s guiding principles provide the foundation for decision making and long term sustainability. They are the lens through which priorities, investments and collaboration models will be assessed. Member centred | Innovation | Scalability | Financial logic | Proactive | Impact Strategic service portfolio The strategic service portfolio is the centrepiece of the GÉANT Association’s future direction. It reflects the association’s commitment to deliver high value, scalable services that meet evolving NREN and R&E user needs while maintaining financial sustainability. It is also diversifying into a complementary set of emerging and professional services to strengthen the human and organisational aspects of the community. Joint design and delivery with NRENs and partners will be reinforced by an effective Product Lifecycle Management system and aligned with an innovation funnel and diversified funding channels. Each of the portfolio areas will ultimately be guided by thematic roadmaps, building on GÉANT’s CTO workshop results where relevant, and each service will have a clear Service Value Statement. Technical services: Network infrastructure | Identity and Access Management (IAM) | Security Emerging services: Data | Education | AI Professional services: Events management | Advisory | Learning and talent development Engagement and partnerships Active engagement and partnerships are what enable and drive GÉANT to build trust, shape policy, expand its reach and co create services with members and partners. As funding opportunities evolve, the GÉANT Association must cultivate a broader and more dynamic partnership model and broaden its ecosystem to integrate new stakeholders from the digital R&E sphere. Engagement is a strategic capability that channels new knowledge, collaborative approaches, donor insights, and a global perspective for R&E service innovation development. Global partnerships The GÉANT Association will maintain and expand strategic partnerships with global Regional Education Networks (RENs) through collaborative projects and mutually beneficial initiatives to extend the value, reach and influence of the GÉANT Association and its members. Influencing and policy engagement The GÉANT Association will be broadly recognised as the secure, trusted, sovereign infrastructure for Europe. Vision, mission, strategy Vision, mission, strategy The GÉANT Association provides and advances the digital infrastructure and services required to accelerate research, education, and innovation for a secure and competitive Europe. Membership The GÉANT Association includes 37 NRENs, NORDUnet, and associates including five Nordic NRENs, KREN, CERN, and ESA. Governance The General Assembly is the GÉANT Association’s highest governing body, consisting of representatives from each member. Projects GÉANT projects drive innovation across networking, Identity and Access Management (IAM), global collaboration and more. Vision and mission The GÉANT Association consists of 43 European National Research and Education Networks (NRENs). For decades, we have been building physical and human networks across Europe and around the world. Our unique collaboration model delivers an unmatched multiplier effect and creates the digital foundation for research and education (R&E) in Europe. Together, and as a trusted partner of the European Commission, we power the knowledge sharing and innovation essential for strengthening Europe’s competitiveness, security, and prosperity. Our vision Powering Knowledge for Europe. Our mission The GÉANT Association provides and advances the digital infrastructure and services required to accelerate research, education, and innovation for a secure and competitive Europe. GÉANT Association Strategy 2026-2030 Strategic goals Collaborate to strengthen physical and human networks across Europe and beyond We will further strengthen collaboration between our unique and diverse human network – the most effective way to achieve not just the highest quality and geographic reach of the physical network, but the advancement of the entire digital foundation for research and education. Create scalable, innovative services prioritised by the community We will identify, co-create, and deliver digital services that integrate emerging technology to comprehensively address community priorities, while linking seamlessly to the digital infrastructure we provide. Build a sustainable financial model We will build a sustainable financial model that allows the GÉANT Association to continue its core operations, expand to new markets and end users, realise healthy service and product life cycles, and thrive in a rapidly advancing and commercially competitive technology landscape. Challenges The challenges we face as the GÉANT Association are not static. These are the current primary uncertainties, challenges or risks, and they will be monitored and updated annually: Geopolitical uncertainty with the risk of fragmentation. A diverse association with a spectrum of needs. A highly uncertain funding landscape. A changing EU regulatory environment​. Evolving technology and user expectations. Transformations To both achieve our strategic goals and mitigate challenges, we strive to reach the following transformations by 2030: Realise platforms for NREN collaboration that facilitate both unity and NREN to NREN mutual benefit.​ Ensure organisational and association resilience through a sustainable business and governance model. ​ Establish and execute a common vision on services and innovation with equal access across Europe and globally.​ Leverage our unique position in Europe to increase visibility and influence policy. ​ Mainstream a proactive mindset and approach to anticipate and mitigate future uncertainties. GÉANT Association Strategy Framework 2026-2030 The GÉANT Association Strategy 2026-2030 is underpinned by this Strategy Framework that further elaborates on the strategy and provides the framework for joint execution by the association . It also supports the creation of roadmaps and annual plans which inform the Annual Operating Plan and Budget. They are the lens through which priorities, investments and collaboration models will be assessed. It reflects the association’s commitment to deliver high value, scalable services that meet evolving NREN and R&E user needs while maintaining financial sustainability. It is also diversifying into a complementary set of emerging and professional services to strengthen the human and organisational aspects of the community. Joint design and delivery with NRENs and partners will be reinforced by an effective Product Lifecycle Management system and aligned with an innovation funnel and diversified funding channels. Each of the portfolio areas will ultimately be guided by thematic roadmaps, building on GÉANT’s CTO workshop results where relevant, and each service will have a clear Service Value Statement.
